style: Product-quality render for a mobile app thumbnail. 3/4 front view, about 20 degrees elevation, subject fills roughly 70% of the shorter side, centred with breathing room. One soft key light upper-left, a rim light from back-right, gentle floor contact shadow. No lens flare, no glow, no bokeh props, no text, no UI, no device frame, no watermark. Faithful to the attached reference: keep the real model shapes and materials; clean up, relight and recompose only.

lighting.prompt: The Khronos Damaged Helmet model (exactly as in the attached reference) lit by three coloured point lights — warm orange from the left, cool blue from the right, a white key above — with visible light falloff on the floor around it. Demonstrates runtime light types.

lighting-lab.prompt: The Khronos Damaged Helmet model (exactly as in the attached reference) under a dramatic golden sunset HDR environment, long soft shadow, warm rim light, the environment visible as a soft blurred backdrop. Demonstrates image-based lighting.

fog.prompt: The Khronos Damaged Helmet model (exactly as in the attached reference) with a dense grey volumetric fog: the near half is crisp, the far side fades into the fog, the floor disappears into haze. Demonstrates distance fog.

camera-gestures.prompt: The Khronos Damaged Helmet model (exactly as in the attached reference) with a thin translucent orbit ring around it and a subtle two-finger pinch gesture hint as faint circles, suggesting orbit, pan and zoom camera controls.

materials.prompt: The Khronos Damaged Helmet model (exactly as in the attached reference) next to a row of five small PBR test spheres showing clearcoat, metal, rough plastic, glass and anisotropic brushed metal. Demonstrates material extensions.

debug-overlay.prompt: The Khronos Damaged Helmet model (exactly as in the attached reference) with a thin wireframe overlay on half of it and a green bounding box, plus faint axis gizmo lines at the origin. Demonstrates debug visualization.

video-recording.prompt: The Khronos Damaged Helmet model (exactly as in the attached reference) slowly turning, with a small red recording dot and a thin white frame corner marks suggesting a video capture in progress. No text.

secondary-camera.prompt: The Khronos Damaged Helmet model (exactly as in the attached reference) viewed from the front, with a small rounded picture-in-picture inset in the top-left corner showing the same helmet from above. Demonstrates a second camera view.

model-viewer.prompt: The battle-damaged sci-fi helmet of the attached reference — this exact model, and no other: a large curved visor of dark teal-green glass carrying faint cyan HUD glyphs, a glowing cyan ring lens and a small orange triangle marker, scuffed off-white armour plates with gold-brass trim along the jaw, and a segmented ear module with ribbed cables tucked behind. Three-quarter front-left view with the visor turned towards the camera, the helmet centred and filling about 70 percent of the frame height, cables kept behind the silhouette, alone on the field with a soft contact shadow. Demonstrates loading and orbiting a glTF model.

two-d-in-three-d.prompt: A wide studio shot in which the whole subject sits well inside the frame, surrounded by empty field on all four sides — it should read as slightly too small rather than crop anything. The subject: the battle-damaged sci-fi helmet of the attached reference — this exact model, teal-green glass visor with a glowing cyan ring, scuffed off-white plates, gold-brass trim — centred on an invisible turntable in three-quarter front-left view, about 45 percent of the frame width. Around it float four small rounded rectangular Compose cards, angled to face the camera, each fully visible with clear empty field between it and the nearest image edge: one upper-left, one mid-right, one lower-left, and one lower-centre in front of the helmet's chin. The first three are annotation labels, each with a short bold title and two lines of small body text; the titles are exactly "Visor", "Vents" and "Shell", and the body text is short plain English about that part of the helmet — never Lorem ipsum, never placeholder Latin. The fourth is a control card carrying a single small rounded pill button. The cards are opaque, high-contrast, crisply legible thin panels with a soft drop shadow, about one third the helmet's width; on a light field they are white with dark text, on a dark field charcoal with white text. No borders, no icons, no other props. Demonstrates Compose UI rendered on quads inside the 3D scene.

custom-geometry.prompt: The trefoil ribbon knot of the attached reference — exactly this shape, a (2,3) torus knot swept by a flat band that twists two and a half turns around the loop and whose width ripples six times along it, so the band passes in front of and behind itself three times. Polished SceneView-blue #005BC1 metal, glossy and slightly reflective, a bright specular highlight travelling along the band where it turns. Floating alone with a soft contact shadow, tilted so the lobes separate instead of reading as a flat rosette. Demonstrates a mesh whose vertices are generated in Kotlin at runtime.

lines-paths.prompt: The closed route of the attached reference — exactly this shape: a loop through eight control points arranged on a circle and lifted by two full sine periods, so it waves up and down twice round the ring. The route is a smooth swept tube of pale blue #A4C1FF with a real thickness and real shading, not a hairline. Eight purple #6446CD beads sit on the control points, a larger soft-lilac #D2A8FF sphere marker rides the route with a slightly fatter lilac trail behind it, and directly below, flat on the ground plane, the same eight points are drawn as a dashed straight-segment polyline in deep blue #005BC1. Seen from about 27 degrees above. No grid, no props. Demonstrates lines, paths, splines and point sets drawn as swept tube geometry.
